input.question: When was the ability to use fossils to date isotope formations developed?
input.context: At the beginning of the 20th century, important advancement in geological science was facilitated by the ability to obtain accurate absolute dates to geologic events using radioactive isotopes and other methods. This changed the understanding of geologic time. Previously, geologists could only use fossils and stratigraphic correlation to date sections of rock relative to one another. With isotopic dates it became possible to assign absolute ages to rock units, and these absolute dates could be applied to fossil sequences in which there was datable material, converting the old relative ages into new absolute ages.

Context:
At the beginning of the 20th century, important advancement in geological science was facilitated by the ability to obtain accurate absolute dates to geologic events using radioactive isotopes and other methods. This changed the understanding of geologic time. Previously, geologists could only use fossils and stratigraphic correlation to date sections of rock relative to one another. With isotopic dates it became possible to assign absolute ages to rock units, and these absolute dates could be applied to fossil sequences in which there was datable material, converting the old relative ages into new absolute ages.

Question:
When was the ability to use fossils to date isotope formations developed?

response.prediction:
The ability to use fossils to **date rock formations** (not isotope formations, but rather the rock layers in which fossils are found) was developed **before the 20th century**, using the principle of **stratigraphic correlation** and the concept of **relative dating**. 

However, the ability to **assign absolute ages to those fossil-bearing rock formations** using **isotopes and radiometric dating** was developed **at the beginning of the 20th century**. Before this, geologists could only determine the **relative ages** of rock layers and the fossils within them by observing their position (superposition) and by comparing fossil assemblages (biostratigraphy).

So, to directly answer your question based on the context:

> The ability to use fossils **to date rock formations relatively** (not absolutely) was developed **before the 20th century**.  
> The ability to use **isotopes to assign absolute ages to fossil-bearing rock formations** was developed **at the beginning of the 20th century**.

If you meant "when was the ability to use fossils together with isotopic dating developed?" then the answer is:  
**At the beginning of the 20th century**, when isotopic dating became available, it became possible to apply absolute dates to fossil sequences that contained datable material.
